pseudos.pseudo: An exceptionally heavy rainy season, a force indifferent to human settlement, reveals the structural vulnerability of communities positioned downstream. The swollen Euphrates becomes an instrument of exposure, flooding the homes, farms, and schools of Deir Ezzor and Raqqa — the very foundations of subsistence and social reproduction. This is not random misfortune but the materialization of a geographic and economic margin, where populations bear the hydrological costs of an upstream nation's water management and a state's limited capacity for preemptive infrastructure investment.

The state's response mobilizes the machinery of sovereignty — the navy deploys boats for evacuation — yet this apparatus arrives as a compensatory measure after the collapse of basic infrastructure, an earthen bridge. The sequence reveals a gap: official warnings are issued, but the material reality they describe outpaces the protective capacity available to the warned. The subsequent negotiation with Turkey, an upstream power, underscores the periphery's lack of control over a vital resource flowing through its territory.

The result is a stark ledger of loss: drowned children, whose vulnerability was neither mitigated by warning nor by infrastructure, alongside widespread devastation to subsistence economies and public institutions. The president's visit to the flood zone performs a ritual of attention, while the substantive power shift — Turkey's agreement to reduce releases — is negotiated between states, beyond the reach of the affected population. The gap persists between the administration of crisis and the lived reality of those who pay its price.

It all began with a single misread weather report in a Damascus office—a forecaster glanced at the decimal point on a precipitation graph and saw 12 millimeters instead of 120. That one-second miscalculation meant emergency warnings for Deir Ezzor were delayed by four critical hours. By the time sirens sounded, the Euphrates had already swallowed the low-lying farms, and the earthen bridge that collapsed under the weight of fleeing residents was already doomed. The children who drowned were, in effect, killed by a misplaced comma in a data file.

No one remembers the loose hinge on the sluice gate at the Tabqa Dam. A maintenance worker, distracted by a phone call about his daughter's school play, forgot to torque a single bolt during the weekly inspection. That tiny oversight meant the gate couldn't seal properly when the upstream rains hit Turkey. The resulting uncontrolled releases forced Syria's navy to scramble boats for evacuations they hadn't planned for, and the extra surge is what finally buckled the earthen bridge in Raqqa. One stray thought about a school play cascaded into a full-scale military rescue operation.

If not for a wrong phone number on a Turkish agricultural ministry memo, the crisis might have been contained. The memo, meant to alert Syrian water authorities about planned upstream releases, was accidentally faxed to a dry-cleaning shop in Gaziantep. By the time the error was discovered, Turkey's reservoirs had already discharged their heaviest flows in three decades into the Euphrates. The delayed warning meant Syria's president was touring the flood zones as a witness to damage that could have been mitigated, while officials issued alerts that arrived, quite literally, after the fact.

During one of the heaviest rainy seasons in three decades, surging flows on the Euphrates flood homes, farms, and schools in Deir Ezzor and Raqqa. An earthen bridge collapses. Several children drown despite official warnings.
After surging flows flood Deir Ezzor and Raqqa, the navy deploys boats for evacuations. Turkey agrees to reduce upstream releases. Syria's president visits the Euphrates flood zones.
Surging flows flood homes, farms, and schools in Deir Ezzor and Raqqa, causing widespread flooding. An earthen bridge collapses, damaging infrastructure. Turkey agrees to reduce upstream releases.

candidates.title: Road Wars
candidates.overview: After the earth’s water supply is depleted, the survivors form roving road gangs, armed to the teeth and desperate to find and protect water supplies. But when a new breed of blood-drinking humans emerges, the survivors must contend with a whole new threat to their existence.

candidates.title: Poem of the Sea
candidates.overview: A Soviet dam project means that many old Ukrainian villages will end up under water. There are conflicts between the dam engineers and villagers who don't want to move.

candidates.title: Flood
candidates.overview: Timely yet terrifying, The Flood predicts the unthinkable. When a raging storm coincides with high seas it unleashes a colossal tidal surge, which travels mercilessly down England's East Coast and into the Thames Estuary. Overwhelming the Barrier, torrents of water pour into the city. The lives of millions of Londoners are at stake.

candidates.title: The Wild Men of Kurdistan
candidates.overview: After dealing with the Shut in the Balkans, Kara Ben-Nemsi ('Karl the German') receives a firman (precious passport) from the padishah (Ottoman sultan) before he continues his travels through Kurdistan. Achmed El Corda, the son of Halef's Hadedhin Beduin tribe's sheik Mohammed Emin, has been captured by the machredsh (Turkish governor) of Mossul for resisting water seizure by his Turkish troops. Kara takes charge of the rescue.

candidates.title: Salvage
candidates.overview: When a container washes ashore the residents of a sleepy cul-de-sac are plunged into violence, terror and paranoia. Ring fenced by the military a single mother must overcome all the odds to save her daughter.

candidates.title: Spitak
candidates.overview: «Spitak» tells the story of the most devastating and largest (in terms of casualties) Armenian earthquake that happened on December 7, 1988. This day went down in history as the day of a horrible disaster, which claimed the lives of over 25,000 lives and left more than half a million people homeless. The film «Spitak» is the story of Gor, who left Armenia in search of a better life but now returns back after the earthquake in order to find his home. His family. But it's too late. Everything is destroyed by the disaster. and he has to re-learn to love what he destroyed himself. Film-Requiem.

candidates.title: Atragon
candidates.overview: The legendary empire of the lost continent of Mu reappears to threaten the world with domination. While countries unite to resist, an isolated World War II Captain has created the greatest warship ever seen, and possibly the surface world's only defense.

candidates.title: Joe the King
candidates.overview: A destitute 14-year-old struggles to keep his life together despite harsh abuse at his mother's hands, harsher abuse at his father's, and a growing separation from his slightly older brother.

candidates.title: Inescapable
candidates.overview: Twenty-five years ago Adib, a promising young officer in the Syrian military police, suddenly left Damascus under suspicious circumstances. Abandoning the love of his life Fatima, he made his way to Canada and wiped the slate clean. When his daughter Muna suddenly disappears in Damascus, his past threatens to violently catch up to him. Teaming up with a Canadian emissary, Adib must now confront the turmoil he thought he left behind in order to find Muna.

candidates.title: Acid
candidates.overview: During a heat wave, strange clouds start pouring down acid rain, wreaking devastation and panic throughout France. In a world teetering on the edge, a girl and her divorced parents must join forces to confront and try to escape this climate catastrophe.

candidates.title: Bravo Two Zero
candidates.overview: When an elite eight-man British SAS team is dropped behind enemy lines, their mission is clear: take out Saddam Hussein's SCUD missile systems. But when communications are cut and the team finds themselves surrounded by Saddam's army, their only hope is to risk capture and torture in a desperate 185-kilometer run to the Syrian border.  Based on the true story of a British Special Forces unit behind enemy lines during the Gulf War, Bravo Two Zero explores the tragedies and triumphs of men taken to the edge of survival in the Persian Gulf War.

candidates.title: Jet Stream
candidates.overview: A TV weatherman tries to prove his theory that a series of unexplained catastrophes are the result of powerful winds found in the upper atmosphere coming down to ground level. His claims attract the attention of government scientists, who need his help to control the phenomena before it destroys all life on Earth (Locatetv.com)
candidates.genres: Action, Adventure, Drama, Science Fiction, TV Movie

candidates.title: Leaving Afghanistan
candidates.overview: 1988-1989. The end of the Soviet-Afghan war. The USSR begins its withdrawal from Afghanistan. Soviet General Vasiliev's son - a pilot named Alexander gets kidnapped by the mujahideen after his airplane crashes. As a result the 108th motorized infantry division's long awaited return home gets put on hold for one last mission: bring the General's son back. Based on true events the previously untold story of the courageous and tragic withdrawal campaign (through the Salang pass) reveals the danger the horror and the complexity of human nature during wartime.

candidates.title: Ustica: The Missing Paper
candidates.overview: On the evening of June 27, 1980, a DC9 of the private airline Itavia disappeared from radar screens without sending any emergency signal. The aircraft, stabilized in cruise at 7.600 meters above sea level, sank into the Tyrrhenian Trench, between Ponza and Ustica. 81 people lost their lives, including 14 children. There are three hypotheses about the disaster, but none has ever been proven, until the analysis of the findings and documentary material reveals a fourth, chilling possible cause of the disaster.

candidates.title: Valley of the Wolves: Palestine
candidates.overview: After the Freedom Flotilla attempts to bring humanitarian assistance to Gaza refuses to turn back, it is attacked by the Israeli military. In a dramatic battle scene, activists resist and are killed by the Israeli soldiers. A Turkish commando team led by Polat Alemdar (Necati Şaşmaz) travels to West Bank in Palestine, where they launch a campaign against Israeli military personnel in an attempt to track down and eliminate an Israeli general, leader Moşe Ben Eliyezer (Erdal Beşikçioğlu), who is the responsible for the flotilla raid.

candidates.title: Bermuda Tentacles
candidates.overview: After Air Force One goes down during a storm over the Bermuda Triangle, the United States Navy is dispatched to find the escape pod holding the President. A giant monster beneath the ocean awakens and attacks the fleet.

candidates.title: I Saw the Sun
candidates.overview: In the southeast region of Turkey, the Kurdish family of Altun lives in a small mountainside village plagued by a 25-year war that makes their daily lives a hellish struggle. As the war intensifies, the family is forced to migrate west to the city of Istanbul.
